meaning: to argue a position you do not necessarily hold, in order to test an idea
example: In the seminar, Maria played devil's advocate to test our conclusions.
origin: From the Catholic Church, where an official argued against a candidate for sainthood

wrong_meanings.meaning: to give up on a debate and stop arguing
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes taking an opposing side on purpose, not quitting the discussion

wrong_meanings.meaning: to speak very quietly so that others cannot hear
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: Nothing in the idiom refers to volume or to being quiet

wrong_meanings.meaning: to agree with everyone to avoid any conflict
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the opposite of the idiom, which means deliberately challenging the group's view

explanation: 'Play devil's advocate' means to take the opposing side in a discussion so that an idea is tested properly. It is common in academic seminars and debates.
